dedupeSummary.rationale: No intra-batch duplicates qualified for collapse. The two findings that share a code location (DEDUP-001 and DEDUP-003 both touch _carryBuffer L191-198) have distinct root-cause classes (DeployedABIDrift fatal revert vs. ConfigDrift silent shrink) and distinct mitigations, so per the keep-both rule they remain separate. The two High DeployedABIDrift findings (DEDUP-001, DEDUP-002) are independent fatal reverts at different call sites — each independently kills the script and each needs its own fix, so collapsing them would drop a second live blocker (Law 1: recall beats tidiness). Findings 3/4/6 have conceptual lineage in the SUPERSEDED route (migrate:ys-swap-deploy / migrate:phusd-minter-deploy) but reconcile per-entryPoint via the folded fingerprint and the InPlaceMigrator/saga-2.1 route REPLACES that route, so they are live again here and are retained with lineage annotations, not dropped.

findings.title: Saga 2.1 reverts against live mainnet: old strategy lacks setAsideBufferRecipient() getter the script calls in _carryBuffer
findings.description: Step 5a (_carryBuffer) unconditionally calls `IYS(oldYS).setAsideBufferRecipient()` on the live old DOLA/USDC strategies (0x90ce274b... / 0x90af002E...). The deployed strategy bytecode PREDATES the global `setAsideBufferRecipient` feature in current lib/vault source — the selector 0x88b57777 is absent, so the staticcall reverts with empty data and aborts the entire script. This is the first of two independent fatal reverts; the script cannot complete (deploy, wire, revoke/grant mint, setMigrator, write handoff) and therefore cannot set up the preconditions 2.2/2.3 require.
findings.impact: The headline operational script is dead-on-arrival against live mainnet state once the allotment tripwire is satisfied. Because step 9 (setMigrator) and the handoff JSON write are downstream of this revert, 2.2 can never run (its preflight requires staker.migrator()==migrator). The migration cannot proceed at all. No funds are lost (it reverts atomically), but the deploy-and-freeze leg is non-functional, blocking the entire saga.
findings.evidence: fork preview (block 25321049): trace shows `0x90ce274b...::setAsideBufferRecipient() [staticcall] -> [Revert] EvmError: Revert` immediately followed by `script failed: <empty revert data>`. Direct cast call of selector 0x88b57777 on the old DOLA strategy also reverts. setAsideBufferSize(staker) on the same contract returns 25 fine, confirming the contract is live but lacks only the newer getter.
findings.recommendation: Do not call setAsideBufferRecipient() on the deployed old strategies. Either (a) drop the live-recipient sourcing and pass the recipient explicitly (the plan/2.3 only ever expect the staker), or (b) wrap the call in a try/catch (staticcall) and fall back to STAKER on revert, or (c) read the recipient via the actual deployed ABI. Add a fork-preview to CI so this surfaces before a Ledger broadcast.
findings.dedupeNote: Shares code location with DEDUP-003 (_carryBuffer L191-198) but distinct root cause (fatal getter-absent revert vs. silent buffer shrink) and distinct mitigation; kept separate. Forms a DeployedABIDrift pair with DEDUP-002 — independent fatal reverts at different call sites; both retained.

findings.title: Saga 2.1 reverts replicating V1 config: deployed PhusdStableMinter V1 stablecoinConfigs is a 4-field struct but the script decodes 7 fields
findings.description: The script's inline `IMinterV1.stablecoinConfigs(address)` declares a 7-value return tuple (yieldStrategy, exchangeRate, decimals, enabled, maxMintPerDay, mintedToday, lastMintTimestamp), matching the CURRENT lib/phUSD-stable-minter source. The DEPLOYED V1 minter (0x435B0A18...) returns only a 4-field struct (yieldStrategy, exchangeRate, decimals, enabled) — raw return is exactly 128 bytes. The 7-field decode expects 224 bytes, so the ABI decoder buffer-overruns and reverts. This independently kills the script in _registerOnV2(USDE) (and would equally kill _registerOnV2(DOLA/USDC) and _v1Strategy). Config replication is the stated purpose of step 7 and cannot execute.
findings.impact: Second fatal revert: even with the buffer-recipient bug fixed, the script still cannot read V1's config and therefore cannot replicate exchangeRate/decimals onto V2 — the exact replication-fidelity guarantee the plan §5.6/§7 promises. The migration leg remains blocked. The underlying values ARE correct (DOLA rate=1e18, dec=18 read fine via the 4-tuple ABI), so this is a pure interface-shape drift, not a value error — but it is fatal as written.
findings.evidence: fork preview: `PhusdStableMinter::stablecoinConfigs(USDe) -> 0x...0de0b6b3a7640000...12...01` (4 words) then `[Revert]`. cast decode of the same call with a 4-tuple ABI succeeds (ys, 1e18, 18, true); with the 7-tuple ABI it fails 'buffer overrun while deserializing'.
findings.recommendation: Change the IMinterV1 interface in the script to the deployed 4-field shape `stablecoinConfigs(address) returns (address,uint256,uint8,bool)` (or use getStablecoinConfig if the deployed bytecode exposes it — it does not in this case). Verify against the deployed bytecode, not the latest submodule source. A fork-preview gate would have caught this.
findings.dedupeNote: Same rootCauseClass (DeployedABIDrift) as DEDUP-001 but an INDEPENDENT fatal revert at a different call site (_registerOnV2 decode vs. _carryBuffer staticcall). Each independently aborts the script and needs its own fix; collapsing would hide a second live blocker that survives fixing the first. Kept; cross-referenced with DEDUP-001 as a drift pair so the report can group them under one 'verify against deployed bytecode' theme.

findings.title: Carried set-aside buffer silently reduced 25% -> 10% (hardcoded constant overrides live config, only logged not asserted)
findings.description: The script comment, the docs (§8) and the SETASIDE_BUFFER_PCT constant all describe 'carry forward the EXISTING 10%'. On the live old strategies the actual set-aside buffer for the staker is 25%, not 10% (confirmed on fork). _carryBuffer reads existingPct purely to log it ('cross-check'), then writes the hardcoded SETASIDE_BUFFER_PCT=10 to the new strategies regardless. The cross-check is never asserted equal, so the 25->10 reduction passes silently. 2.3 then asserts ==10, locking in the reduced value as if intended.
findings.impact: The new strategies will withhold only 10% of staker surplus as a below-par reserve instead of the 25% the live system currently uses — a 60% reduction in the staker's set-aside cushion against negative-yield dips. The 'carry forward the existing' intent is violated; the documented assumption (existing == 10%) is factually wrong against current mainnet state. This is an unknowing config drift the operator would be surprised by (a footgun): they believe they are replicating the live buffer, but they are shrinking it.
findings.evidence: fork: oldDolaYS.setAsideBufferSize(staker)==25, oldUsdcYS.setAsideBufferSize(staker)==25. Script line 61 `SETASIDE_BUFFER_PCT = 10` with comment 'carry forward the existing 10%'. Preview log: 'old buffer % (cross-check): 25 recipient: ...' then setSetAsideBuffer(staker, 10).
findings.recommendation: Either source the buffer pct live (newYS.setSetAsideBuffer(STAKER, existingPct)) so it truly carries forward, or assert require(existingPct == SETASIDE_BUFFER_PCT, 'buffer drift') so the mismatch reverts loudly instead of silently shrinking the reserve. Confirm with the operator whether 10% or 25% is the intended post-migration buffer; update the doc's '10%' claim either way.
findings.dedupeNote: Same code location as DEDUP-001 (_carryBuffer L191-198) but distinct root cause (ConfigDrift silent shrink vs. DeployedABIDrift revert) and distinct mitigation (assert/source-live vs. fix-the-ABI); kept separate per keep-both rule. LINEAGE: conceptually mirrors the OPEN Low 'set-aside buffer 25%->10% downgrade' from the superseded migrate:ys-swap-deploy route; does NOT auto-collide (different entryPoint, folded fingerprint) and is LIVE AGAIN on this replacing route, so retained. Report should cross-reference the superseded-route lineage.

findings.title: New ERC4626YieldStrategy instances and minter V2 are deployed without a pauser (left unpausable)
findings.description: AYieldStrategy._pauser defaults to address(0) and pause() is onlyPauser, so a strategy with no pauser set can never be paused (pause() always reverts: msg.sender != address(0)). PhusdStableMinter likewise deploys with pauser==address(0) and pause() requires msg.sender==pauser. Script 2.1 deploys ysDolaV2, ysUsdcV2 and minterV2 and never calls setPauser on any of them. Once 2.2 sets these as the live DOLA/USDC strategies and the active phUSD minter, the protocol's global-pauser break-glass does not cover them.
findings.impact: The new live yield strategies and the new minter cannot be paused in an incident until the owner remembers to call setPauser post-hoc. emergencyWithdraw (owner-only, no whenNotPaused) still works, so funds are recoverable, but the standard pause circuit-breaker is absent on the contracts that will hold all DOLA/USDC principal. This is an operational-availability footgun, not a direct loss. Scope note: 2.2/2.3 do not set the pauser either, so it is not deferred-by-design — it is simply missing from the runbook.
findings.evidence: Source: AYieldStrategy onlyPauser modifier + setPauser never invoked anywhere in the three saga scripts (grep). PhusdStableMinter.pause() requires msg.sender==pauser, pauser unset at construction. Preview confirms no setPauser call in the trace.
findings.recommendation: Add setPauser(globalPauser) for ysDolaV2, ysUsdcV2 and minterV2 in 2.1 (or explicitly in 2.2 before unpause), sourcing the live pauser the same way 2.2 captures staker.pauser(). Document the intended pauser in the runbook checklist.
findings.dedupeNote: Not tool noise: fork-confirmed operational-availability footgun on contracts that will hold all DOLA/USDC principal, with explicit not-deferred-by-design verification. LINEAGE: mirrors the OPEN Lows 'replacement strategies deployed without pauser registration' + 'new minter deployed without pauser' from the superseded route; per-entryPoint fingerprint means no auto-collision and the issue is live again on the saga-2.1 route. Retained with lineage; QA-report candidate.

findings.title: Script has no post-condition assertions: mint-authority swap, setMigrator, and wiring are fire-and-forget
findings.description: Unlike 2.2 (_postAssert) and 2.3 (_verify), script 2.1 asserts NOTHING after its writes. It fires setMinter(V1,false)/setMinter(V2,true), setMigrator(migrator), all setClient/setWithdrawer/registerStablecoin calls, then only console.logs a summary. There is no `require(phUSD.minters(V2))`, no `require(!phUSD.minters(V1))`, no `require(staker.migrator()==migrator)`, no `require(minterV2.isStablecoinRegistered(DOLA))`. The most consequential state change in the script — moving phUSD mint authority — is unverified.
findings.impact: If a setter silently no-ops or the phUSD `setMinter` ABI differs on the deployed token (a real risk given the two confirmed ABI drifts above), the script would 'succeed' while leaving phUSD with the wrong mint authority — potentially nobody able to mint, or V1 still able to mint a frozen liability. The broadcast then patches mainnet-addresses.ts pointing the world at a misconfigured minterV2. Asserting the end state is the cheap insurance the CLAUDE.md configuration-safety gate demands.
findings.evidence: Source review: run() ends at _printSummary (log only); no require after line 160 setMigrator. Contrast 2.2 _postAssert / 2.3 _verify which do assert. The two fork-confirmed ABI drifts show deployed-vs-source shape mismatches are a live hazard for exactly these fire-and-forget calls.
findings.recommendation: Add a post-write assertion block to 2.1 mirroring 2.2/2.3: verify V2 granted & V1 revoked on phUSD, staker.migrator()==migrator, both new strategies have staker+minterV2 as clients and accumulator as withdrawer, and minterV2 has DOLA/USDC/USDe registered with the replicated rate/decimals. Refuse to write the handoff JSON / patch addresses unless they hold.
findings.dedupeNote: Distinct from DEDUP-001/002 (those are concrete fatal reverts; this is the absence of a verification gate that would have caught such drifts on the fire-and-forget setMinter/setMigrator writes). Unique insight tying the missing asserts to the CLAUDE.md config-safety gate; not tool noise. No superseded-route lineage. Retained; QA-report candidate.

findings.title: 2.1 is not idempotent / has no progress guard: a re-run redeploys everything and re-revokes/re-grants phUSD mint
findings.description: Unlike the project's documented checkpoint pattern (progress.<chainId>.json) and unlike 2.3 (which guards every accumulator add/remove on isRegisteredStrategy for idempotency), 2.1 has no progress file and no 'already deployed?' guard. Re-running it (e.g. after a partial broadcast failure, or an operator re-running the npm script) deploys a SECOND set of migrator/strategies/minterV2, transfers another allotment, and re-fires setMinter(V1,false)/setMinter(V2_new,true) and setMigrator(newMigrator) — silently overwriting the handoff JSON with the new addresses and orphaning the first deployment.
findings.impact: A double-run during the time-pressured migration session points 2.2/2.3 at a different minterV2/strategies than were granted/wired in the first run (or grants mint to a minterV2_2 while the addresses.ts patch and any external integrator still reference minterV2_1). Because the only safe ordering is back-to-back, an accidental re-run is a realistic operator footgun that produces a hard-to-debug split-brain. Not a fund loss, but an availability/consistency hazard during the most fragile window.
findings.evidence: Source: no vm.readFile/progress guard in 2.1; _writeDeployments overwrites DEPLOYMENTS_JSON unconditionally on each broadcast. Contrast 2.3's isRegisteredStrategy guards and the project CLAUDE.md 'Resilient Deployment Pattern'.
findings.recommendation: Gate 2.1 on a progress/handoff check: if saga2-deployments.json already exists with valid addresses, refuse to re-deploy (or require an explicit --force). At minimum assert the handoff file does not already exist before writing, so a re-run aborts instead of silently overwriting.
findings.dedupeNote: Distinct root cause (no checkpoint/idempotency guard) from the missing-asserts finding DEDUP-005, with its own split-brain mitigation. LINEAGE: mirrors the OPEN Low 'non-idempotent deploy / no resume checkpoint (YS-35)' from the superseded route; per-entryPoint fingerprint means no auto-collision and the saga-2.1 route reintroduces the hazard. Retained with lineage; QA-report candidate.
